Gonia · Erechtheion building accounts · 408/7 BCE

Seven names,
one uneven obol.

Selected entry: 100 drachmas. IG I³ 476, lines 235–242. This document includes your allocation and the edited record, even if you had not yet revealed it in the activity.

Divide the total. Then read the record.

Six obols make one drachma. 600 obols divided among seven names gives 14 dr. 1 ob. each, with 5 obols left over. This activity permits one extra whole obol per name. 21 distributions balance that total within these rules.

The seven names

Simias Σιμίας

Living in Alopeke. The residence formula identifies where he lives. This entry does not call him an Athenian citizen.

IG lines 236–237: 14 dr. 2 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 2 obols = 86 obols.

Name 1 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Kerdon Κέρδον

No further identifier here. A name alone does not establish legal status. Keep Kerdon’s status unspecified in this excerpt.

IG lines 237–238: 14 dr. 2 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 2 obols = 86 obols.

Name 2 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Sindron Σίνδρον

Of Simias; interpreted as enslaved. The possessive name is interpreted as an enslaved worker’s owner, rather than a father, in the current IG and AIO readings. The Greek does not spell out a word for ‘slave’ here.

IG lines 238–239: 14 dr. 2 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 2 obols = 86 obols.

Name 3 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Sokles Σοκλῆς

Of Axiopeithes; interpreted as enslaved. The owner named for Sokles is Axiopeithes, not Simias. An amount recorded beside his name does not tell us who took possession of the payment.

IG lines 239–240: 14 dr. 2 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 2 obols = 86 obols.

Name 4 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Sannion Σαννίον

Of Simias; interpreted as enslaved. The possessive identifier links Sannion with Simias. The record gives a payment entry, without reporting working hours, personal receipt or living conditions.

IG lines 240: 14 dr. 2 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 2 obols = 86 obols.

Name 5 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Epieikes Ἐπιείκες

Of Simias; interpreted as enslaved. Epieikes’s second amount is one obol below the first five entries. That small difference is compatible with dividing a total into whole obols; the inscription gives no reason for the choice.

IG lines 240–241: 14 dr. 1 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 1 obols = 85 obols.

Name 6 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Sosandros Σόσανδρος

Of Simias in the first entry; interpreted as enslaved. The first entry supplies the possessive ‘of Simias’. The second repeats the name without that identifier. Keep the two entries visible rather than silently inserting words into the second.

IG lines 241–242: 14 dr. 1 ob.

14 drachmas × 6 + 1 obols = 85 obols.

Name 7 in the selected team; this order does not assign individual flutes to people.

Read four working words

Reading aids join words split across lines and use ordinary Unicode Greek. They retain selected older Attic spellings; οἰκῶν and Σοκλῆς show long vowels in the later alphabet. They are not a diplomatic transcription. The licensed XML and scanned pages retain the edition’s restoration brackets.

ῥαβδόσεος

rhabdoseos · for fluting. A genitive of ῥάβδωσις, the cutting of vertical channels. The older spelling corresponds to later ῥαβδώσεως. The heading appears at IG line 192, above the first selected entry.

οἰκῶν

oikōn · living, residing. A present participle modifying Simias: ‘living in Alopeke’. This reading aid uses ω; the stone’s older Attic alphabet writes Ο for this sound. Residence is not a statement of citizenship.

Σιμίο

Simio · of Simias. A possessive genitive after a worker’s name. Its old Attic ending -ο corresponds to later -ου. Modern editors interpret this identifier as ownership here. It is not a separately written word meaning ‘enslaved’.

ἑχσῆς

hechsēs · next in sequence. The source’s older spelling corresponds to later ἑξῆς. With ‘the next [column]’, it orders the work entries. It does not divide particular flutes among the named workers.

What the account can establish

These are two selected entries for column-fluting work in the Erechtheion accounts, 408/7 BCE, not a complete building budget or a daily wage table. The totals 90 and 100 drachmas are sums of the edited individual amounts. Equal division with whole-obol adjustments is a modern arithmetic comparison; it does not establish the ancient accountant’s intention. No amount is converted into modern money. A payment entered beside an enslaved worker’s name does not establish that the worker personally received or controlled it.

Parts of names and numeral signs are restored by editors. The exact sums are exact arithmetic on that edited reading, rather than proof that every sign survives. The current IG and AIO ownership interpretation takes precedence over Caskey’s 1927 English translation, which renders possessive identifiers as family relationships. No modern AIO translation is reproduced here.

The 1927 p. 412 table interprets repeated work stages and distinguishes preserved from restored totals. Its proposed complete-column cost is not used as a measured total or as the budget for this activity.

  • Attic Inscriptions Online, IG I³ 476, translation and commentary by Stephen Lambert and Robin Osborne. Linked for comparison and interpretation; their translation is not bundled.
  • Acropolis Museum, EM 6667 δ, the account fragment’s object record. The printed pages below are an edition, not photographs of the stone.
